what_its_for: Auranofin is used to treat rheumatoid arthritis. It helps reduce joint pain, swelling, and stiffness. It belongs to a group of medicines called gold compounds, which work by calming down your immune system to reduce inflammation in your joints.
how_to_take: Take auranofin by mouth, exactly as your doctor prescribed. You can take it with or without food. Swallow the capsule whole with a full glass of water. Try to take it at the same time each day to help you remember. Do not crush, chew, or open the capsules.
dosing: The usual starting dose is one 3 mg capsule twice a day (morning and evening), or one 6 mg capsule once a day. After several months, your doctor may increase your dose to 9 mg per day if needed. Never change your dose on your own — always follow your doctor's instructions.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is still the same day. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses at once to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store auranofin at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not use it after the expiration date on the label.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking antacids or other medicines that may interact with auranofin without checking with your doctor or pharmacist first. Limit alcohol, as it may increase the risk of stomach upset or liver problems. Avoid prolonged sun exposure and use sunscreen, as auranofin can make your skin more sensitive to sunlight. Do not receive any live vaccines while taking this medicine without talking to your doctor.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you notice any of the following: unusual bruising or bleeding, mouth sores or ulcers, skin rash or itching, yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice), dark or foamy urine, severe stomach pain or diarrhea, shortness of breath or cough, swelling of your legs or feet, signs of infection such as fever or chills, or any unusual changes in how you feel. These could be signs of serious side effects that need prompt attention.
when_it_works: Auranofin works slowly. Most people do not notice improvement for at least 3 to 6 months after starting treatment. It is important to keep taking it even if you do not feel better right away. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor, because stopping suddenly can cause your symptoms to come back.
special_populations: Older adults may be more sensitive to the side effects of auranofin, especially kidney problems or skin reactions, so regular check-ups are important. Auranofin should NOT be used during pregnancy because it can harm an unborn baby — talk to your doctor about effective birth control while using this medicine. It is also not recommended while breastfeeding, as it may pass into breast milk. Children: safety and effectiveness in children have not been well established, so use in children should only be decided by a doctor.
